prompt.en: Which change would NOT make a planned two-metre path beyond the normal range scale more credible?

text.en: Putting the antennas higher with a clearer horizon
Finding stable lower-atmosphere layering along the route
Budgeting for weak redirected energy rather than a clean local path
Treating rare ionospheric openings as guaranteed daily infrastructure

explanation.en: Height, lower-atmosphere enhancement, and scatter link budgets can all help explain difficult VHF paths. Rare ionospheric openings are not dependable daily infrastructure for a routine service.

prompt.en: A VHF event changes from second-long reflected bursts during a shower to a steadier path along a weather boundary. What operating prediction follows?

text.en: Use long overs during the burst period, then shorten messages only after the path becomes steady
Keep burst-period messages highly structured, but allow more normal exchanges during the steadier path
Switch to lower HF for both events because VHF timing no longer matters
Assume both paths will remain open for the same length of time once the first contact is made

explanation.en: Brief reflected bursts reward short structured exchanges. A steadier lower-atmosphere path can support more normal contact timing while the enhancement lasts, but it still should not be treated as permanent coverage.

prompt.en: An operator investigating a weak, smeared HF signal near the path MUF writes, 'Use a wider signal and aim a UHF dish at storm clouds, because lower-atmosphere water vapour is the main HF skip-gap mechanism.' What is the main error?

text.en: The note should use a lower antenna because all smeared signals are local ground-wave signals
The note should blame ordinary line-of-sight blockage instead of any redirected energy
The note mixes a VHF/UHF lower-atmosphere mechanism with HF skip-gap multipath, and wider signals may make distortion worse
The note should raise the frequency above the MUF so the signal bends more strongly

explanation.en: HF skip-gap reception is about small amounts of energy arriving over mixed sky-wave paths near the usable limit. A wider signal can suffer more selective distortion, and UHF weather-related redirection is a different planning problem.
